A LITTLE TRANSPARENCY

A memory, interpreted.
Never a certainty.

Whiffy runs fresh OpenPOM predictions on a Python backend. The deployment reports how many checkpoints it uses (one by default). Each molecule has 138 predicted odor-label scores. Matching rewards wanted notes and penalizes unwanted notes.

  • Matching scores are ranking values, not recreation accuracy or scent intensity.
  • OpenPOM predicts individual molecules—not perfumes, household ingredients, or blends.
  • It cannot recover the chemicals that were actually in a memory or assess safety.
  • Household references are curated sensory exercises. Perfumes are ranked separately using brand-published notes.
  • Some SMILES leave stereochemistry unspecified. Results may miss differences between isomers.
  • The original model’s reported benchmark is not a measured accuracy score for Whiffy.

Your submitted memory is sent to the Whiffy backend and its configured LLM provider. The LLM extracts scent notes and selects candidate molecules from a verified catalog. OpenPOM scores those molecules during the request; a final LLM uses that evidence to select approved home references and sourced perfumes. No simulated result replaces a failed service. Google sign-in is handled by Supabase. Saved memories are stored under your account with database rules restricting access to their owner. Voice input uses your browser’s speech service, which may send audio to its provider. Whiffy does not store recordings. Product images may load from brand image services, and shopping links open external sites. Drafts are not saved to the shelf unless you choose Save.
